theater: 尼羅河三角洲東岸阿瓦利斯

battle.name: 對西克索人的征服
battle.theater: 尼羅河三角洲東岸阿瓦利斯
battle.brief: 前十六世紀末，底比斯王朝起兵收復被西克索人占據的尼羅河三角洲。卡莫斯沿河北上，襲破阿瓦利斯南面的兵營而未能入城；雅赫摩斯一世經多次戰役攻下阿瓦利斯，再越西奈追至沙魯亨，圍城三年取之。攻防兩端靠的都是埃及步兵列陣時的束柄銅矛，本卡這件早王朝長矛即是同型兵器。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 交戰的兩方，是尼羅河谷南北分裂的兩個政權。南方是底比斯的第十七王朝，以及其直接繼承者——雅赫摩斯一世開立的第十八王朝；北方是占據三角洲的西克索人聯盟，其核心是第十五王朝的六位國王，以孟斐斯為首都、阿瓦利斯為夏宮，麾下是三角洲東部的第十六王朝眾多「王子」，以及受其庇護的埃及依附者。第十二王朝約前1786年崩解之後，第十三王朝虛弱，國家分裂，伊特陶伊這座「兩國的控制者」只勉強守住三角洲南端，西部沼澤另有第十四王朝自立，上埃及的第十七王朝則在底比斯另立正統。底比斯與西克索之間長期維持著半商半貢的關係：底比斯的使者可以通行中埃及、在三角洲放牧，西克索一方則以豬肉與穀物回贈，雙方並非一開始就處於交戰狀態。西方文獻中的西克索聯盟也並非一個統一帝國，巴勒斯坦、克里特與美索不達米亞出土的相關器物，都可以只用當時的商路來解釋，不必假想曾存在過一個橫跨西亞的牧羊人帝國。雅赫摩斯一方的軍隊由底比斯駐軍、尼羅河上游的徵召兵、北盟友的援軍，以及來自努比亞的盟軍組成，法老自任全軍統帥，並兼阿蒙神廟的最高祭司；西克索方面則以外來閃族戰士為主力，配備自西亞帶入的複合弓與雙輪戰車，並靠本地徵召的依附者補充兵源。
countriesEn: The two belligerents were two regimes separated by the valley of the Nile. In the south stood the Seventeenth Dynasty of Thebes and its direct successor, the Eighteenth Dynasty founded by Ahmose I. In the north stood the Hyksos confederation occupying the Delta, whose core was the six kings of the Fifteenth Dynasty: their capital was Memphis, their summer residence was Avaris, and under them sat the many princes of the Sixteenth Dynasty in the eastern Delta together with the Egyptian dependants they protected. The Twelfth Dynasty ended about 1786 BC, the Thirteenth was weak, and the state fell apart: It-tawy, the controller of the Two Lands, held only the southern edge of the Delta, the western marshes had a dynasty of their own in the Fourteenth, and the Seventeenth Dynasty in Upper Egypt had set up its own legitimate line. For a long time Thebes and the Hyksos stood in a half-trade, half-tribute relationship: Theban envoys could travel through Middle Egypt and graze cattle in the Delta, and the Hyksos sent back pigs and grain, so the two were not at war from the start. The Hyksos confederation recorded in Western sources was never a single empire either, and the Hyksos-related objects dug up in Palestine, Crete and Mesopotamia can be explained entirely by the trade routes of the time without postulating a shepherd-kings empire stretching across western Asia. Ahmose's army was built from the Theban garrison, levies from the upper Nile, auxiliaries from the northern allies and Nubian contingents, with the pharaoh as commander-in-chief of the whole force and at the same time the high priest of Amun. On the Hyksos side the army was made up chiefly of foreign Semitic warriors equipped with the composite bow and the two-wheeled chariot brought in from western Asia, and was reinforced by Egyptian dependants levied locally.
people: 這場戰爭的時序骨架由五個人撐起。第一位是塞克南雷·陶二世，第十七王朝的君主，在外交上對西克索人極硬，頭部受過傷，今日的木乃伊存於開羅博物館，那道傷痕可能正是某次小規模襲擊的紀念；他與西克索王阿波比同時在位。第二位是他的兒子卡莫斯，第十七王朝的末代君主，也是真正開戰的人：在位第三年他整備船隊，率軍自底比斯沿尼羅河北上，出其不意攻破西克索人在南部的兵營，直抵阿瓦利斯城下，卻未能入城，只毀掉城郊田地；他在底比斯的石碑上記下這次勝利，也記下截獲阿波比致努比亞求援信使的經過。第三位是阿波比，第十五王朝末代之王，傳說他曾致書底比斯要求拆掉河馬池以免吵到他安睡，而正是他在雅赫摩斯一世在位的前半段失位。第四位是雅赫摩斯一世，第十八王朝的建立者，在位約二十五年，登基之後並未立即恢復北伐；關於他作戰的細節主要來自上埃及艾爾卡比的軍人雅赫摩斯的墓誌，這位軍人出身於當地世襲的總督家族，父親在塞克南雷·陶二世軍中已經服役。第五位正是這位士兵雅赫摩斯，他徒步跟隨國王的戰車衝鋒——這是埃及史料第一次提到馬與戰車——屢次俘獲敵兵，三度獲賜「勇敢金」，在阿瓦利斯陷落後分得一名男子與三名女子共四名俘虜，並參與了對沙魯亨的圍城。背景人物是公元前300年左右的祭司曼內托，他寫的埃及史記載了西克索人攻入孟斐斯，是今日所知這場戰爭最早的敘述；他的書只剩殘篇，靠後人引述流傳下來。
peopleEn: The skeleton of the sequence is carried by five men. The first is Sekenenre Tao II, king of the Seventeenth Dynasty, extremely hard on the Hyksos in his diplomacy; his head was wounded, and his mummy, kept in the Cairo Museum, still bears the scar, possibly the record of some small raid. He reigned at the same time as the Hyksos king Apophis. The second is his son Kamose, the last king of the Seventeenth Dynasty and the man who actually opened the war: in the third year of his reign he fitted out a fleet, marched north from Thebes along the Nile, caught the Hyksos off guard, broke their southern barracks and came right up to the walls of Avaris, yet failed to take the city and did no more than destroy the fields around it; on a stele at Thebes he recorded that victory and also the capture of a messenger Apophis had sent to Nubia for help. The third is Apophis, the last king of the Fifteenth Dynasty, who in legend wrote to Thebes demanding that the hippopotamus pools be filled in so that their noise would not keep him asleep in far-off Avaris, and who lost his throne in the first half of the reign of Ahmose I. The fourth is Ahmose I, founder of the Eighteenth Dynasty, who reigned about twenty-five years and did not at once resume the war in the north on his accession; the details of his fighting come chiefly from the tomb inscription of a soldier named Ahmose at El-Kab in Upper Egypt, a man from a family that had long governed that district and whose father had already served under Sekenenre Tao II. The fifth is that soldier Ahmose himself, who followed the king's chariot on foot into the fighting, the first mention of horse and chariot in Egyptian records, who took enemy prisoners repeatedly, was awarded the gold of valour three times, and after the fall of Avaris received one man and three women, four prisoners in all; he also took part in the siege of Sharuhen. The background figure is Manetho, a priest of about 300 BC whose history of Egypt records the Hyksos taking Memphis and is the earliest account of this war that survives; only fragments of his book remain, preserved through quotation by later writers.
kits: 本卡兵器是埃及長矛：早王朝時期把銅或青銅矛頭束在木杆上的步戰長矛，埃及人用它守住城垣的缺口。本卡這件兵器屬於早王朝的形制，而這場戰爭開打時已是前十六世紀，埃及步兵所用的仍是同一類束柄銅矛，只是矛頭更薄、杆身更長，是當時攻擊力最穩定的一種冷兵器；換言之，征討西克索人的埃及軍隊，其骨幹裝備與本卡同型。埃及方面的配備還包括：拉力較弱的埃及式弓、銅斧、短刀、投石索、銅箭鏃，木框蒙皮的長方形大盾，以及攻城用的土坡與填壕器械。馬匹與戰車在這批埃及傳世材料中首次出現，士兵雅赫摩斯跟隨國王戰車即是明證。相對地，西克索人帶來的是他們真正的技術優勢：更短更強的複合弓、雙輪輕戰車（由馬拉動）、騎兵與馬上射擊、金屬頭盔、鏈環與連綴的甲片、新式盾牌、更銳利的劍與匕首，以及一批改進的箭鏃。這些裝備後來被埃及全盤吸收，成為新王國遠征的技術底子。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the Egyptian spear: a foot weapon of the Early Dynastic period, with a copper or bronze head socketed onto a wooden shaft, used by the Egyptians to hold the gaps in their fortification walls. The piece on this card is Early Dynastic in form, but by the time this war was fought Egypt was in the sixteenth century BC, and the Egyptian foot soldiers still carried the same class of socketed copper spear, only thinner in the head and longer in the shaft, and it was the most reliable close-combat weapon of the age; in other words, the backbone equipment of the Egyptian army that campaigned against the Hyksos was of the same type as the piece on this card. The Egyptian equipment list also included the Egyptian bow, weaker in draw, copper axes, short knives, slings, copper arrowheads, large rectangular shields of wood frame covered in hide, and the ramps and fill for ditches used in siege. Horses and chariots appear for the first time in this body of Egyptian written material, and the soldier Ahmose following the king's chariot is the proof. Against that, the Hyksos brought the genuine technical advantage: a shorter, stronger composite bow, a light two-wheeled chariot drawn by horses, cavalry and shooting from horseback, metal helmets, chain and scale armour, new-style shields, sharper swords and daggers, and a batch of improved arrowheads. All of this was later taken over wholesale by Egypt and became the technical foundation of the New Kingdom's campaigns.
tactics: 這場戰爭可以分成三段樣式不同的作戰。第一段是卡莫斯的奇襲：他先整頓船隻，順尼羅河北下，選在對方毫無戒備的時候切入金字塔形的兵營體系，數日之間連下幾座南部要塞，把守軍逐向北捲；兵營被拔掉之後，他進逼阿瓦利斯，卻因守備森嚴而未能取城，遂改以毀田與斷路代替攻城——他特意奪取西部沙漠的一處綠洲，企圖切斷阿瓦利斯與努比亞之間的南北通道，再沿河返回底比斯。第二段是雅赫摩斯的正面攻堅：埃及軍隊靠密集的步兵縱隊推進，以盾牆與長矛正面頂住守軍的車兵與弓手，弓手在前列投射，戰車由側翼掩護，最後由車兵衝入缺口追擊潰兵；阿瓦利斯是在多次戰役之後才陷落的。第三段是追擊與圍城：埃及人越過西奈追入巴勒斯坦南部，包圍沙魯亨這座堡壘，以壘土、斷援與填平壕溝困之，前後三年才克；同類的圍城在當時的西奈與迦南邊境是常法，攻城方靠的是耐心與糧水供應，而不是一次突擊。整體而言，埃及方面的戰術核心是步行步兵的列陣與城下的工程戰，並以河運與綠洲維持遠征補給；西克索方面則以車兵突擊與弓手近射為主，一旦失去阿瓦利斯這座夏宮與三角洲的基地，便無從退守。
tacticsEn: This war can be divided into three phases fought in three different ways. The first is Kamose's surprise: he first fitted out his fleet, went down the Nile, chose the moment when the enemy was least alert and cut into the pyramid-shaped system of barracks, taking several southern fortresses in a matter of days and rolling the defenders northward. With the barracks gone he pressed on to Avaris, but the city was too well defended to be taken, so he substituted the destruction of fields and the cutting of routes for an assault: he deliberately seized an oasis in the western desert to break the line of communication between Avaris and Nubia, and then returned to Thebes along the river. The second phase is the frontal assault under Ahmose: the Egyptian army advanced in dense columns of foot, held the enemy's chariotry and archers head-on with shield wall and spear, put the archers in front to shoot, covered the flank with the chariots, and finally sent the chariot corps through the breach to run down the fugitives; Avaris fell only after several engagements. The third phase is the pursuit and the siege: the Egyptians crossed Sinai in pursuit into southern Palestine and laid siege to the fortress of Sharuhen, hemming it in with earthworks, cutting its supplies and filling its ditches, and it took three years to reduce; sieges of this kind were standard practice on the Sinai and Canaanite frontier of the day, and the besiegers relied on patience and on the supply of food and water rather than on a single rush. Taken as a whole, the tactical core on the Egyptian side was the deployment of foot soldiers and the engineering of the siege below the walls, with river transport and the oases keeping the army supplied on campaign; on the Hyksos side it was the charge of the chariot and the close shooting of the archers, and once Avaris, that summer residence, and the Delta base were lost there was nowhere left to fall back to.
data: 可以核對的數字大致如下。年代上，第十二王朝約在前1786年結束，內弗爾霍特普一世約在前1740至前1730年在位，其弟兼繼承者索貝克霍特普四世時期西克索人出現在三角洲，約前1720年占領阿瓦利斯；第十五與第十六王朝在通行編年下約跨前1674至前1548年；第十五王朝的六位國王合計統治約一百零八年。雅赫摩斯一世的年表分歧較大：一般作前1558至前1533，另有前1550至前1525一說，多數學者認為他在位約二十五年，最早一份與他相關的正式記載出現在其第二十二年；本卡所用的前1523年，是戰爭列表為此役所記的年份，宜視為整場戰役收束的標記，而不是某一次會戰的確切時日。阿瓦利斯陷落的年份同樣有兩說，或在雅赫摩斯第四年，或在第十五年。沙魯亨的圍城歷時三年。軍人雅赫摩斯在戰役中三度獲賜「勇敢金」，在阿瓦利斯陷落後分得一名男子與三名女子共四名俘虜。地理上，阿瓦利斯即今提爾達巴，位於尼羅河三角洲東部、北緯三十點八度與東經三十一點八度一帶；底比斯（今盧克索）在北緯二十五點七度；沙魯亨在巴勒斯坦南部。埃及民用曆為三百六十五天，十二個月各三十天外加五日閏日，歲首定於汛期初，故本卡所標的第3月只能對應到現代九至十月的北上開戰時節，文獻並無確切月日記載。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. On dating: the Twelfth Dynasty ended about 1786 BC; Neferebre I reigned about 1740 to 1730 BC, and it was in the reign of his brother and successor Sobekhotep IV that the Hyksos appeared in the Delta, occupying Avaris about 1720 BC; the Fifteenth and Sixteenth Dynasties span about 1674 to 1548 BC in the chronology normally used; the six kings of the Fifteenth Dynasty are thought to have ruled for about a hundred and eight years in all. The chronology for Ahmose I varies more: usually given as 1558 to 1533 BC, with an alternative of 1550 to 1525 BC, and most scholars hold that he reigned about twenty-five years, the earliest formal reference connected with him falling in his twenty-second year; the year 1523 BC used on this card is the one the list of wars assigns to this campaign, and is best taken as a marker for the closing of the whole war rather than the exact date of any single battle. The year of the fall of Avaris is likewise given in two versions, either the fourth or the fifteenth year of Ahmose. The siege of Sharuhen lasted three years. The soldier Ahmose was granted the gold of valour three times in the campaign, and after the fall of Avaris he received one man and three women, four prisoners in all. On geography: Avaris is the site of Tell el-Dab'a, in the eastern Delta near 30.8 degrees north and 31.8 degrees east; Thebes, modern Luxor, lies at 25.7 degrees north; Sharuhen was in southern Palestine. The Egyptian civil calendar had 365 days, twelve months of thirty days each plus five epagomenal days, with the year beginning at the start of the inundation, so that the third month marked on this card can only be equated with the modern September-to-October season in which the northern campaigns were opened; the sources give no exact day or month.
cause: 把這場戰爭的起因拆開看，是三層原因疊在一起。最底層是結構性的崩解：第十三王朝在伊特陶伊只能勉強統治三角洲南端，西部沼澤另有第十四王朝自立，孟斐斯對中埃及的控制名存實亡；上埃及的第十七王朝既已另立正統，兩邊的界線只剩下尼羅河一道。就在這個真空裡，來自敘利亞與巴勒斯坦的閃族部落分批遷入東埃及，逐步接管城鎮，並由首領奪取王位、沿用埃及王號，這就是第十五王朝的起源——現代研究多認為那不是一次武裝大入侵，而是數十年間的和平滲入與逐步接管。中層是關係的惡化：西克索人雖與底比斯有貿易與進貢往來，卻把北方的亞洲人視為神聖土地上的污穢，兩方往來書信裡充滿不平等的語氣；傳說中阿波比甚至要求底比斯拆掉河馬池，以免吵到他安睡——這段傳聞背後的史實背景，大概只是當時埃及分裂的現況。最上層是直接導火索：卡莫斯在位第三年抱怨自己被北面的亞洲人與南面的努比亞人夾在中間，兩者都占據著他的埃及，他的願望是拯救埃及、粉碎亞洲人；底比斯方面的顧問也曾勸說不要輕易打破與北方共存的好日子，理由是對方的良田在為底比斯耕種、牛群在三角洲吃草、還送來豬——正是這種日常的依賴，讓開戰成為一件需要下定決心的事。
causeEn: Taken apart, the origins of this war are three causes piled on one another. The deepest is a structural breakdown: the Thirteenth Dynasty could hold only the southern edge of the Delta from It-tawy, the western marshes had a dynasty of their own in the Fourteenth, and Memphis's hold over Middle Egypt was nominal; the Seventeenth Dynasty in Upper Egypt had already set up a separate legitimate line, so all that divided the two was the river itself. Into the vacuum left there, Semitic groups from Syria and Palestine moved into eastern Egypt in successive waves, took over the towns by degrees, and eventually a chief seized the kingship and took up the Egyptian royal titulature, which is the origin of the Fifteenth Dynasty; modern research holds that this was not a single armed invasion but a peaceful infiltration and a gradual take-over spread across several decades. The middle layer is the souring of relations: although the Hyksos traded with and paid tribute to Thebes, they regarded the Asians in the north as a stain on the sacred soil of Egypt, and the correspondence between the two courts was full of unequal language; legend has it that Apophis even demanded that the hippopotamus pools at Thebes be filled in so their noise would not disturb his sleep, and the historical background of that story is most likely only the divided condition of Egypt at the time. The top layer is the immediate trigger: in the third year of his reign Kamose complained that he was caught between the Asians in the north and the Nubians in the south, both of whom occupied his Egypt, and his wish was to save Egypt and crush the Asians; Theban advisers likewise urged against breaking the comfortable coexistence with the north, on the grounds that the best of their fields were being farmed for Thebes, that their cattle grazed in the Delta, and that they sent on pigs. It was precisely this daily dependence that made going to war a decision that had to be taken deliberately.
impact: 對埃及，這場戰爭的直接成果是國家的重新統一與新王朝的開端。雅赫摩斯一世建立了第十八王朝，此後三百餘年間法老自居全境唯一的統治者，底比斯重新對孟斐斯與三角洲收稅、徵兵、任官。軍事技術層面的影響更為長遠：西克索人帶進來的複合弓、雙輪輕戰車、馬匹與騎兵，經雅赫摩斯時代吸收之後，成為新王國往西奈與黎凡特遠征的技術底子，第十八王朝此後對赫梯的戰爭與對敘利亞的遠征，都建立在這批新裝備之上。制度上，第十七王朝末年已在底比斯建立常備兵與地方募兵的編制，戰後整軍把河谷防務與三角洲駐軍重新編排，軍隊從此有了固定的番重與按季節出徵的習慣。另一面則是破壞性的：底比斯人把北方的亞洲統治者視為惡人，戰後系統地拆毀他們留下的建築與紀念物，連文字痕跡也一併抹去，因此今日關於西克索人的直接材料極少，我們所知的形象多由曼內托的引述與後世書寫塑成；這段被刻意抹除的過去，在近代敘事裡被重組成牧羊人王的野蠻故事，影響直到今天仍然存在。
impactEn: For Egypt the direct outcome of this war was the reunification of the country and the opening of a new dynasty. Ahmose I founded the Eighteenth Dynasty, and for the more than three centuries that followed the pharaoh stood as the sole ruler of the whole land, and Thebes resumed collecting taxes, taking levies and appointing officials in Memphis and the Delta. The effect on military technology was the more durable: the composite bow, the light two-wheeled chariot, the horse and the mounted man brought in by the Hyksos, once absorbed in the age of Ahmose, became the technical foundation of the New Kingdom's campaigns into Sinai and the Levant, and the later war against the Hittites and the Syrian campaigns of the Eighteenth Dynasty both rest on that new equipment. Institutionally, the Seventeenth Dynasty had already set up a standing force and a system of local levies at Thebes by its end, and the reorganisation of the army after the war remapped the defence of the valley and the garrisons of the Delta, giving the army fixed companies and a habit of campaigning by season. The other side of it is destructive: the Thebans treated the Asian rulers of the north as wicked men, and after the war they systematically pulled down the buildings and monuments they had left behind and wiped out even their written traces, which is why so little direct material about the Hyksos survives and the image we know was shaped by the quotations of Manetho and by later writers; that deliberately erased past was reassembled in modern narrative into the story of barbaric shepherd kings, and that influence is still with us.
result: 結果是西克索人在埃及的統治終結。卡莫斯未能取下阿瓦利斯，卻拔掉了西克索人在南部的兵營，逼其放棄中埃及、退守三角洲；阿波比在雅赫摩斯一世在位的前半段失位，第十五王朝崩解，第十六王朝的眾多王子隨之失去依托；孟斐斯與阿瓦利斯重歸埃及王權。雅赫摩斯一世在多次戰役之後終於攻下阿瓦利斯，埃及軍隊隨即越過西奈，追入巴勒斯坦南部，圍困沙魯亨三年而取之，西克索人的殘部從此退回西亞。戰爭列表把前1523年記為這場征服的年份，正落在雅赫摩斯統治後期與第十八王朝建立的銜接處，可視為戰役收束與新秩序落成的標記。結果的深處不在攻城，而在繼承：西克索人的武器技術、馬匹與車兵編制被征服者原封不動地接過，北方亞洲人在埃及的政治存在則被徹底清除，埃及從此以上下埃及之王的號自居，向西奈與黎凡特重新伸手；而本卡這件早王朝的束柄銅矛，也在這條脈絡裡被新王朝的步兵一路帶進了敘利亞的高原。
resultEn: The result was the end of Hyksos rule in Egypt. Kamose did not take Avaris, but he tore out the Hyksos barracks in the south and forced them to abandon Middle Egypt and fall back on the Delta; Apophis lost his throne in the first half of the reign of Ahmose I, the Fifteenth Dynasty broke up, and the many princes of the Sixteenth Dynasty lost the support they had stood on; Memphis and Avaris returned to Egyptian kingship. After several engagements Ahmose I at last took Avaris, and the Egyptian army crossed Sinai in pursuit into southern Palestine, besieged Sharuhen for three years and took it, and the remnants of the Hyksos withdrew to western Asia. The list of wars records the year 1523 BC for this conquest, which falls at the junction between the later years of Ahmose's reign and the establishment of the Eighteenth Dynasty, and can be read as the marker for the closing of the campaign and the settling of a new order. The heart of the result lies not in the siege but in the inheritance: the Hyksos weapon technology, their horses and their chariot organisation were taken over by the conquerors untouched, while the political presence of the northern Asians in Egypt was wiped out completely; Egypt henceforth styled itself king of Upper and Lower Egypt and reached out again towards Sinai and the Levant. And the socketed copper spear of the Early Dynastic period on this card was carried along that same line by the infantry of the new dynasty, as far as the highlands of Syria.
